lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: ask about wait time, seating, local style, and whether a place is touristy
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Ask a local which nearby lunch spot they genuinely use and why.
lessons.title: Choosing a neighborhood lunch place
lessons.objective: Ask a local where they usually eat lunch, then check wait time, available seats, and whether a place serves local food.
lessons.focus: 近く means nearby; いつも行きますか asks about a person’s usual choice. 待ち時間 asks the wait. 観光客が多い describes a place with many tourists, while 地元の人 describes locals.
lessons.scene: Sam asks a local for a lunch recommendation near the station.

cards.ja: 待ち時間はどのくらいですか
いつもここで食べますか
どの店がおすすめですか
地元の人がよく行きます
この店は観光客が多いですか
cards.en: Does this place have many tourists?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。駅の近くで、どの店がおすすめですか。
reader.en: Excuse me. Which place near the station do you recommend?

reader.speaker: Local
reader.ja: 角の定食屋がおすすめです。
reader.en: I recommend the set-meal restaurant on the corner.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: いつもここで食べますか。
reader.en: Do you usually eat here?

reader.speaker: Local
reader.ja: はい。地元の人がよく行きます。
reader.en: Yes. Local people often go there.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: この店は観光客が多いですか。
reader.en: Does this place have many tourists?

reader.speaker: Local
reader.ja: いいえ、あまり多くありません。
reader.en: No, not very many.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 待ち時間はどのくらいですか。
reader.en: How long is the wait?

reader.speaker: Local
reader.ja: 今はほとんど待ちません。
reader.en: There is almost no wait now.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 空席はありますか。
reader.en: Are there any seats available?

reader.speaker: Local
reader.ja: はい、ありますよ。
reader.en: Yes, there are.

speaking.opening: こんにちは。何かお探しですか。
speaking.goal: Ask which nearby place the local genuinely uses, whether it is busy with tourists, how long the wait is, and if seats are available.
speaking.closure: 教えてくれてありがとうございます。

lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: ask about courses, set menus, portions, and what is available today
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Have a server explain the fixed-price lunch and what choices it includes.
lessons.title: Understanding the lunch set
lessons.objective: Ask what today’s lunch set includes, which main dishes are available, whether a drink comes with it, and how large the portion is.
lessons.focus: 〜には何が付いていますか asks what comes with a set. 含まれていますか asks whether a drink is included in the stated price. 主菜 means main dish, and 量 asks about portion size.
lessons.scene: Sam asks a server to explain the choices in today’s fixed-price lunch.

cards.ja: 飲み物は含まれていますか

cards.en: Can I choose the main dish?

cards.ja: 今日のランチセットには何が付いていますか
cards.en: What comes with today’s lunch set?

cards.ja: 鶏肉のセットをお願いします

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 今日のランチセットには何が付いていますか。
reader.en: What comes with today’s lunch set?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: スープと主菜とデザートが付きます。
reader.en: It comes with soup, a main dish, and dessert.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 飲み物は含まれていますか。
reader.en: Is a drink included?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、お茶か水が含まれています。
reader.en: Yes, tea or water is included.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 主菜は選べますか。
reader.en: Can I choose the main dish?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい。鶏肉か魚を選べます。
reader.en: Yes. You can choose chicken or fish.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 量は多いですか。
reader.en: Is the portion large?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 普通の量です。
reader.en: It is a regular portion.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: では、鶏肉のセットをお願いします。
reader.en: Then the chicken set, please.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: かしこまりました。
reader.en: Certainly.

speaking.role: Guest reading the lunch set menu
speaking.opening: 本日のランチセットはいかがですか。
speaking.goal: Have the server explain the set, ask what comes with it, whether a drink is included, the portion size, and choose a main dish.
speaking.closure: 鶏肉のセットをお願いします。

lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: identify fillings, sauces, spice, portion, and whether to eat there or walk
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Order a regional street-food specialty from a busy counter.
lessons.title: Ordering takoyaki at a street stall
lessons.objective: Ask what takoyaki contains, choose a portion and sauce, check the spice level, and say whether it is to eat here or take away.
lessons.focus: 屋台 is a street stall. たこ焼き is an Osaka specialty with octopus inside. 〜が入っていますか asks about filling; ソースは辛いですか asks about heat. ここで食べます and 持ち帰りです distinguish eating here from taking it away.
lessons.scene: Sam orders takoyaki from a busy street stall.

cards.note: A cooked Osaka street-food specialty with octopus pieces inside.

cards.ja: ねぎ抜きでお願いします
たこ焼きを一皿お願いします
もう一度お願いします

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。たこ焼きには何が入っていますか。
reader.en: Excuse me. What is in the takoyaki?

reader.speaker: Vendor
reader.ja: たことねぎが入っています。
reader.en: It has octopus and green onion.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ソースは辛いですか。
reader.en: Is the sauce spicy?

reader.speaker: Vendor
reader.ja: いいえ、あまり辛くありません。
reader.en: No, it is not very spicy.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 小サイズを一つ、ねぎ抜きでお願いします。
reader.en: One small serving, without green onion, please.

reader.speaker: Vendor
reader.ja: はい。ここで食べますか、持ち帰りですか。
reader.en: Certainly. Will you eat here or take it away?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 持ち帰りです。
reader.en: It is to go.

reader.speaker: Vendor
reader.ja: 少々お待ちください。
reader.en: Please wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。
reader.en: Thank you very much.

speaking.role: Guest at an Osaka street-food stall
speaking.opening: いらっしゃいませ。たこ焼きはいかがですか。
speaking.goal: Ask about the filling and sauce, order a small serving without green onion, and say it is to go.
speaking.closure: 持ち帰りです。ありがとうございます。
